title: Cairo's Undead Melting Pot
summary: A huge city open to Kindred of every sect.

claims.text: Cairo counts some 200 known vampires and is open to Kindred whatever their sect, and a safe haven for the clanless.
The city is Camarilla ground more in name than in fact; the label holds mostly because the Sabbat does not openly contest it.
By old edict any vampire may enjoy the prince's welcome and protection, so long as the newcomer presents properly on arrival.
Mukhtar Bey has held the domain since first claiming it in 1406.
Under Ottoman rule Mukhtar Bey spread influence beyond Egypt and came to be called Prince of Cairo, partly to please the rulers' new European allies.
The prince's strictest law guards the Mogamma: no vampire under the prince's authority may meddle with the state or local government or its officers.

title: The Khittas
summary: The quarters of Cairo held by Kindred families.

claims.text: Only part of the city is khitta-held; the busy downtown core, called Free Cairo, is where most immigrant vampires live.
The prince does not usually force khitta residents to accept strangers into their domains.
Visitors with the prince's leave to stay may feed discreetly in the open remainder of the city.
The Assamite Antara built a khitta when the Abbasid capital rose, as a base for the clan's growth in Egypt.
